text: On the P30 (Kirin 710) the service's Release AOT build runs on Mono (.NET 10.0.14) with AdvSimd=False, AdvSimd.Arm64=False, Dp=False and only Vector128.IsHardwareAccelerated=True. The PTQ1_0 kernel did a 6144x2048 product in 382 ms scalar and 226 ms Vector128: about 0.03 tokens/s per thread for the 2B. ARM intrinsics are not an option under Mono; the C# kernel needs a different design (lookup tables) or a runtime that exposes NEON.

text: A Release build of src/CircleAIService with -p:EnableLLVM=true (Mono LLVM AOT, runtime .NET 10.0.14, android-arm64) builds and installs, then every start of the service aborts within half a second on the P30: Mono assertion aot-runtime.c:5341, condition plt_entry not met, on whichever thread first calls through the PLT (.NET Timer, a thread-pool worker, the main thread). Circle AI in the foreground kept rebinding it, so it crash-looped every ~4 s until the 28 Oct v62 build was put back with adb install -r. The kernels stay on Mono's non-LLVM AOT; do not retry EnableLLVM without a new reason and the owner's nod.
subject: build:android-aot
challenge: Can Mono LLVM AOT speed up the C# PTQ1_0 kernels on the P30?

text: PTQ1_0 6144x2048 product on one P30 thread inside the service (Release, Mono non-LLVM AOT, .NET 10.0.14), 2026-10-30: Scalar 383 ms, Vector128 226 ms, Table 42.3 ms, Lut 8.24 ms (0.334 GB/s, ~0.78 tok/s for the Bonsai 2 2B on one thread). The block-by-block lookup table (Ptq1Lut.MatVec, commit 6be79bb) is Mono's kernel path. Under Mono a Vector128 byte shuffle costs 7.38 ns and a Vector128 add 7.36 ns in a dependent chain: every vector op is that slow there, so vector kernels cannot beat the scalar table on this runtime.
subject: engine:kernels
challenge: Which PTQ1_0 kernel path is fastest on the P30 under Mono?

text: PTQ1_0 6144x2048 Lut product on the P30 across threads (Mono, WorkerPool, commit 4ad8b58), table build included per pass, 2026-10-30: 1 thread 10.75 ms, 2: 4.41, 3: 3.65 (best, 0.754 GB/s, ~1.76 tok/s for the 2B's products), 4: 4.51, 5: 3.88, 6: 4.31, 7: 5.09, 8: 4.74. More than 3 threads gets worse. The 2048-wide table build takes 0.91 ms on one thread, a quarter of the 3-thread time. Single-thread Lut measured 9.80 ms this run against 8.24 ms an hour earlier: expect ~20% run-to-run spread on this phone. Mono's ceiling for the 2B looks like ~2 tok/s; NEON (CoreCLR) is the lever past it.
subject: engine:threads
challenge: How far do threads take the C# PTQ1_0 product on the P30 under Mono?

text: The owner decided on 2026-10-30 to keep the managed engine on Mono (the shipped Android runtime) and not to try CoreCLR on Android for now, after seeing Mono's ceiling for the C# PTQ1_0 product on the P30 (best 3.65 ms per 6144x2048 at 3 threads, ~1.8 tok/s for the 2B's products). Speed work stays inside Mono's limits: scalar lookup tables, threads, fewer instructions per lookup.

text: The C# qwen35 model (Qwen35Model, commit 25ce41f) matches the pinned fork on the Bonsai 2 2B: over fixtures/bonsai2/2B/logits.json (12 prompts x 32 steps, teacher-forced) all 384 greedy tokens equal the fork's and the largest top-20 logit difference is 0.249; the parity test holds 0.3. On the Windows dev PC in Release on 8 threads: 9.1 tok/s, loaded in 155 ms. Remaining for the S2 checkpoint: sampling, ManagedChatGenerator, one build site wired, then the 2B answering on the P30.
subject: engine:model
challenge: Does the C# Bonsai 2 engine produce the fork's tokens?

text: The C# engine's ManagedChatGenerator (c575a16) answers through IChatGenerator exactly as the pinned fork does: through the interface, prompts render to the fork's text and ids, and greedy replies equal the fork's (greet 32 tokens Length; chinese 20 and system 14 Stop at <|im_end|>), 18 of 18 on both legs in Release. The persona is a real system turn (system messages merged into one, first). A recurrent model (Gated DeltaNet) cannot step back, so the state keeps ONE mark where the last turn began: the next turn's prompt matches up to it (the template writes a reply back without the think block it was generated after), and sessions are saved at that mark. Reused, restored and cold second turns give the same answer.
subject: managed engine

text: A kernel that sweeps its rows once per block needs chunks that fit in the cache. Ptq1Lut.MatVecRows is block-major (one block's tables hot in L1 while every row in the chunk uses them), and the chunk was rows/(threads*4): for the 2B's tied output head (248,320 rows) that made 9 MB chunks, re-read from RAM on each of 16 sweeps, so on the P30 the head cost 1.09 s a token, 3.2x its share of the weights, and decode (0.50 tok/s) ran at half of prefill (1.08). Capping a chunk at 256 KB of weights (3d490e1) took decode to 0.94 tok/s and the desktop parity run from 5.45 to 6.96 tok/s, bit-identical. Symptom to recognise: decode slower than prefill per token, when the only extra work is the head.
subject: managed engine kernels

text: The 2B answers on the P30 through C# (3b099ae, 2026-10-31): adb shell am broadcast -a com.bhengubv.circleai.action.SOAK -n com.bhengubv.circleai.service/ai.circle.SoakReceiver --es do engine [--es text ...] [--ei max 48]. It loads the 2B from the store or the sideload folder /sdcard/Android/data/com.bhengubv.circleai.service/files/models/Ternary-Bonsai-2-2B/Ternary-Bonsai-2-2B-PTQ1_0.gguf (push it from PowerShell, then sha256sum on the phone), asks with AssistantPersona.Prompt as the system turn, greedy, and logs under CircleAI.Engine. Result: word for word the desktop's answer; load 3.8-4.6 s; prefill 1.04 tok/s (81 tokens in 78 s, token by token); decode 0.94 tok/s; 96 s instead of 78 when asked within a minute of a reinstall (service start-up competes). The P30's logcat holds about two minutes, less than a run: collect lines as they arrive.
subject: managed engine p30

text: The pinned fork (prism-b10743-adfffbe) prefills on the CPU through its FUSED gated_delta_net op, not the chunked DeltaNet form: delta-net-base.cpp's build_delta_net takes build_delta_net_fused for more than one token when cparams.fused_gdn_ch is set, and llama-context.cpp resolves fused_gdn_ch (and fused_gdn_ar) to true whenever the fused op and its layer sit on the same device - every CPU-only run. So the C# engine's token-by-token recurrence IS the fork's prefill form; the plan's 'port the chunked form for parity' item is answered without porting (read 2026-11-01).
subject: managed-engine

text: S2's build site is wired: AIService.BuildByEngine builds ManagedChatGenerator for ModelEngine.Managed (the row's engine, or AIOptions.Engine when a host names one); ShippedEngines always includes Managed and EngineChoice/DeviceModelAssessor admit only qwen35 in PTQ1_0 for it. The inference process takes 'engine' in its load request (WorkerWire.Engine), and the soak 'engine' broadcast now loads a model THERE and asks it once through InferenceSupervisor.AskOnceForTestAsync - '--es engine LlamaCpp' times the native fork on the same path. No catalogue row is Managed yet (S4 switches the Bonsai rows).
subject: managed-engine

text: Before the C# engine answers real questions on the P30: the supervisor ends the worker after 90 s with no progress (NoProgress) and the C# 2B read an 81-token prompt in 78 s, the service's own prompt being longer; and AIService's warm-up prefill is not reused by the first question (the state can only rewind to where the last turn began). Primed starts (S3) and a progress signal during prefill are what fix it. The phone was disconnected on 2026-11-01, so the worker-path timing and the fork's timing on the P30 are still owed.

text: The C# engine holds a tool call to the Qwen3.5 template's XML form (<tool_call>/<function=>/<parameter=>) from the token after the model writes <tool_call>: ToolCallGrammar masks the logits, the shortlist first and the whole vocabulary only when none fits. The 2B given get_weather writes the call well formed and ends the turn. ToolCallReader still reads JSON only, so an XML call is not acted on until S8 passes tools natively.
subject: managed-engine

text: S3 measured on the 2B against the fork, teacher-forced over all 12 x 32 fixtures (289 steps judged): working memory Off 289 (drift 0.25); 4-bit Mse keys 289 (1.05), Prod keys 286 (2.87); 3-bit Mse 282 (2.57), Prod 280 (4.63); 2-bit Mse 276 (5.35), Prod 270 (7.38). The MSE form beats TurboQuant's second stage at every width on attention, so keys take Mse; AIService builds the C# engine at 4 bits by default (a quarter of fp16's memory, every fork token kept). TurboKvCacheTests pins it.
subject: managed-engine

text: TurboQuant version-2 payloads: HadamardRotation (seeded signs + Walsh-Hadamard blocks, a seeded permutation for non-power-of-two widths; the transform is WalshHadamard, which PrismHadamard now calls) reconstructs exactly as the dense rotation did (MSE 0.117/0.0345/0.0094 at 2/3/4 bits) at O(d log d); QjlProjection is the second stage (one sign bit a coordinate of a seeded Gaussian projection of the residual). Version-1 payloads and the ports' parity are unchanged. KvCompressionMode moved into CircleAI.Core.
subject: turboquant

text: Primed starts (S3): ManagedChatGenerator keeps the state after the system turn - in memory (Qwen35State.MarkPrimed) and on disk under <temp>/CircleAI/primed (the app's cache on Android), at most 4 files, named by engine numerics, model identity (length + SHA-256 of the first MB), KV mode, capacity and the system turn's tokens. The next conversation with that system turn resumes 'primed' or 'primed-disk'; AIService keeps the system turn to the persona alone, so the warm-up primes the first question. Desktop: a 39-token prompt's prefill 2.8 s cold, 1.3 s primed. Bump EngineNumerics whenever the engine's arithmetic changes.
subject: managed-engine
